This leads to another interesting line of thought: this could kick the can down the road one step when it comes to the matter/antimatter asymmetry of the visible universe. Perhaps in the beginning, all mass (or close to it) was dark matter, and baryonic matter, photons, and all the other things we require for our existence was created by dark matter annihilation. This process might be highly asymmetric and favor "matter". Rather than the line I've heard frequently about matter and anti-matter being of very similar quantities in the early universe, and that what is left is the result of an imbalance of about one part per billion, perhaps it's all explained by the products of dark matter annihilation.

Of course we'd still have to explain the mechanism for this asymmetry, but considering how little we know about the nature of dark matter itself, it may make sense to figure we'll get to that when we know enough to even start making guesses.
